survey: A wooden barrel stands upright on a plank floor in front of a yellow patterned wall. The camera is a little above the barrel's top. The lid is an open ellipse seen from above, set inside a raised rim of stave ends. Four dark metal hoops wrap the body, each with one rivet at the front. All the hoops bow downward like ellipses seen from above, and the lower hoops bow more, which is correct for a camera above the object. The staves run vertically and get narrower and closer together toward the left and right edges as the surface turns away, and they follow the barrel's bulge. The bottom hoop and the base sit flat on the floor, and the cast shadow falls to the right along the floor. The floor planks run diagonally toward the back right and meet the wall along a slanted line, which reads as a room seen from slightly above and rotated a little. That fits the downward view of the barrel's top. Because the barrel is round, it looks the same from any rotation, so its symmetric front view does not conflict with the angled floor. The lid ellipse, the hoop curves, the floor and the contact with the floor all agree on one camera.
